newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end firmer on buoyant turnover.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end firmer on buoyant turnover.

text.p: Broad-based institutional and emerging retail demand combined to push turnover in Singapore's stock market to one of the highest levels seen in the last three years, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index climbed 30.04 points to 2,254.68 on a hectic volume of 771.8 million shares. The last time the exchange saw such turnover was in 1993 when it hit 770 million.
Rumours about the health of China's leader Deng Xiaoping in mid-afternoon also spurred profit-taking in Malaysian issues traded over-the-counter (OTC), which cooled the UOB OTC index.
The index finished at 1,313.10, down 9.4 points, off from a new high of 1,343.09 points.
Dealers said high turnover was fanned by speculation, aided by improved business forecast for various industrial sectors.
"The rumours caused the Hong Kong market to have a blitz, and it filtered here," a dealer with a local brokerage said, referring to the sharp drop in the Hang Seng Index.
Gainers led losers 393 to 94. Leading gainers were Oriental Holding which ended up Singapore $1.00 to S$14.20 and City Development warrants, which rose S$0.40 to S$12.50.
